source: Rich Mix public Spektrix v3 API (no credentials, no auth headers)

requests.reduction: REDUCED from 354 events (262 FILM) to 40 (31 FILM): every event referenced by a future instance, plus 30 FILM controls that have no future instance. The subset preserves the shape that matters — a populated film catalogue against an almost empty film calendar. sha256 above is of the FULL 387 KB response, not committed.

note: No pagination headers were returned (no Link / Content-Range) and content-length equalled the body, so instances.json is the COMPLETE RESPONSE BODY that endpoint returned for that query. That is an HTTP-level fact only. It does NOT establish that the response is the venue's exhaustive future inventory: the Spektrix v3 pagination/limit contract was NOT verified against vendor documentation, and an endpoint can return a complete body that is itself a truncated or filtered view.
scopeLimit: A 2026-09-09 observation. It does NOT establish what the source held on 2026-09-08, so it cannot show the baseline run's extraction was correct or incorrect. It also does not establish a CAUSE for the low film denominator: an unpublished calendar, a changed publishing route, or a discovery fault reachable another way all look the same from here. Why film instances stop at 2026-08-27 is unresolved.

independentDiscoveryCheck.why: Six per-event API samples cannot rule out the venue having moved its film programme to a different publishing route. This check uses a route independent of the Spektrix API.
independentDiscoveryCheck.result: 53 URLs. Exactly ONE /cinema/<detail> page: https://richmix.org.uk/cinema/premiere-we-set-the-house-on-fire — the same single film the Spektrix API returned. Also 7 /live-events/<detail> pages, consistent with the API's 9 LIVE instances.
independentDiscoveryCheck.establishes: The venue's own CMS publishes one cinema detail page, so the website is not advertising a film programme that our API route is missing.
independentDiscoveryCheck.doesNotEstablish: That no other publishing route exists anywhere, nor any cause. The /cinema/ listing page itself is client-rendered via Spektrix web components and server-returns no showtimes, so it could not be counted directly without a browser.
